conclusion: The misstatement is the interest of AUD 48.53 accrued to 30 September 2026 that the bank confirms for the Business Savings Account and the books have not recorded; it arose in the current period. It is factual: the bank's confirmation states the amount, so there is no doubt about it. There is no indication of fraud: an unrecorded period-end accrual of interest in the company's favour is an omission of a routine adjustment.

reasoning_chain.text: GL account 091 shows AUD 11,581.23 at 30 September 2026.

The bank's reply confirms a balance of AUD 11,581.23 at 30 September 2026, states that no interest was credited to the account in the period, and states accrued interest of AUD 48.53 at that date, in the customer's favour and not yet credited to the account.

A factual misstatement is one about which there is no doubt; a judgemental misstatement arises from management judgements, such as accounting estimates, that the auditor considers unreasonable (ASA 450 para A6).
When the auditor identifies a misstatement, the auditor evaluates whether it is indicative of fraud (ASA 240 para 36).
The interest earned to the period end is confirmed by the bank and not recorded in the books, so the misstatement is factual and arose in the current period.
Omitting a small accrual in the company's own favour gives no indication of fraud.

counter_argument: A reply showing that the interest had already been credited, or a period-end accrual recorded elsewhere, would remove the misstatement.
